Finding 2, step 1 of 3: the verdict can now be read through methods only. Only crates/review-domain/src/repo_scope/resume.rs changed; no field was removed or renamed and no behaviour changed.

Four accessors added beside the fields of Resume, each returning an owned answer - the shape a derived view can keep when step 3 makes the verdict one disposition per position and the fields go:
  pub fn to_read(&self) -> Vec<usize>
  pub fn carried(&self) -> Vec<usize>
  pub fn already_read(&self) -> Vec<usize>
  pub fn skipped(&self) -> Vec<(usize, CarriedSkip)>
kept() -> Vec<KeptRow> is unchanged. A method and a field may share a name in Rust, so every current reader keeps compiling: the oracle still reads verdict.to_read and verdict.skipped as fields until step 2 migrates it. Owned Vec, not a slice, is deliberate: a derived view over one disposition sequence cannot hand out a borrowed slice, so these signatures survive step 3 unchanged. The doc comment on the accessors says to read the verdict through them, never through the fields.
